case_name: Karan Batla and Ors. v. State of NCT of Delhi and Anr. & Ors.

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner husband and respondent wife got married in 2015, had a child, but started living separately in 2017. Wife filed FIR under sections 498A/406/34 IPC. Trial is pending. Parties have settled their disputes and agreed to dissolve marriage by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: The extraordinary power under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure should be exercised sparingly and with great care and caution.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court continuously observed that the extraordinary power Under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure should be exercised sparingly and with great care and caution and can be used to prevent abuse of the process of the court or to secure ends of justice and the exercise of inherent powers entirely depends on facts and circumstances of each case.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their disputes.

outcome.final_order: FIR bearing no. 259/2018 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC is quashed.
